_comment_signature: Deterministic dedup gate thresholds for signature.py. Two anomalies merge into one Business Candidate only if buyer_bucket and function_class both match AND (at least min_shared_function_keywords of the matched function_class's own keywords appear in both groups' text, OR one of the Jaccard floors below is met on workaround/failure wording). min_shared_function_keywords=2 (not 1) because a single generic shared word like 'cost' or 'budget' recurs across unrelated topics often enough to be coincidence rather than corroboration - see README's false-positive controls section.
_comment_lifecycle: Minimum distinct-source counts required to advance state. min_sources_investigate intentionally matches Constraint Archaeology's own --min-independent-sources default (3), so a candidate cannot reach INVESTIGATE on less independent corroboration than CA itself requires before evaluating an anomaly.
_comment_severity: Keyword buckets are intentionally generic (not tuned to any one theme, e.g. AI/quota) so the same rubric applies to any future evidence domain.
_comment_taxonomy_dedup: Every function_taxonomy list below is deduplicated so no entry is a literal substring of another entry in the SAME bucket (e.g. 'credit' is dropped in favor of keeping just 'credit', which already substring-matches 'credits' too; 'manually' is dropped because 'manual' already matches it). Without this, a single word like 'manually' would silently satisfy min_shared_function_keywords=2 on its own by counting as both 'manual' and 'manually' - exactly the false-merge bug the real corpus run caught (see README's false-positive controls section). Substring matching still catches every inflected form; only the redundant duplicate list entries are removed.
